newsitem.title: USA: Formulab Neuronetics launches neural PC.
newsitem.headline: Formulab Neuronetics launches neural PC.

text.p: Formulab Neuronetics Corp Ltd introduced a new computer and software that it said mimics the human brain and can process more complex problems than existing personal computers.

It said the new computer, called the Richter Paradigm Computer, uses dozens of reduced instruction computing set (RISC) processors and performs computations at much faster speeds than a PC running an Intel Corp Pentium processor running at 166 megehertz.
The company, based in Perth, Australia, unveiled software, a new computer, and a card that connects to a standard PC.

The Neurocard, which can be inserted or attached to a personal computer, can convert a PC instantly into a "reasoning" machine. But unlke the PC, the Richter Paradigm Computer is not designed for general purpose computing, but for areas where reasoning can be used, such as stock picking.
The company sells the computer separately, which can be expanded to became as powerful as a parallel supercomputer.
The new computer starts at $3,000, the card is available for $300 and the software is $90. The system can be expanded by adding more processors, encased in a hexagon-shaped disk.
